title: Probabilistic Newman lemma with ordinary local confluence
formal: For a probabilistic abstract rewriting system on a countable set, do almost-sure termination from every state under every reduction strategy and ordinary local confluence of the lifted multidistribution relation imply that all reductions from the same state have the same limiting distribution on normal forms?
definitions:
Each rule a→mu assigns a finitely supported probability distribution mu on the countable state set A; a state may have many rules. A normal form has no rule. A multidistribution is a finite multiset [p_i a_i] with p_i>0 and sum p_i≤1; distinct occurrences of the same state are retained separately. In one lifted step, every nonnormal occurrence p_i a_i chooses a rule a_i→mu_i and is replaced by occurrences with weights p_i mu_i(b). Every normal occurrence is kept unchanged. The output is the multiset union, without merging equal states. This defines ⇒; ⇒* allows finitely many steps including zero.

Ordinary local confluence means that for every finite multidistribution m and every pair m⇒s and m⇒t, some finite multidistribution u satisfies s⇒*u and t⇒*u as equal multisets. Joinability only of eventual limits is not the hypothesis. Strategies may choose a different rule for each occurrence and depend on the entire reduction history. Every nonnormal occurrence must advance each round; arbitrary stalling is not permitted.

For a sequence m_0⇒m_1⇒… and normal z, let ell(z) be the increasing limit of the total weight of occurrences of z in m_j. Almost-sure termination means sum_z ell(z)=1 for every such sequence starting at [1a], for every a. The conclusion is pointwise equality of ell(z) for any two sequences from the same [1a]. No bound on expected stopping time is assumed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the implication, or a countable system satisfying ordinary local confluence and the stated universal almost-sure termination with two reductions having different normal-form limit distributions. A counterexample satisfying only limit-joinability does not refute this statement.
context: Faggian distinguishes finite joinability from joinability at the limit. Remark 4.7 explicitly leaves the ordinary-local-confluence candidate unresolved, whereas a weaker limit-local version is already refuted.
why: This asks for a probabilistic counterpart of a fundamental normalization principle.
